description:
Settled 2026-11-11 with no code change (user approved closing).

runtime/src/heap/gc/forward.rs copies a scalar-box root with copy_scalar_box_to_space and writes no forwarding marker, so two roots naming one box would get two 16-byte copies. That is correct: scalars (int, float, atom) have no identity in fz, so equal copies are indistinguishable.

A marker cannot go in the box as laid out. A box (Heap::box_any_value_ref, heap/imp.rs ~294) holds the raw payload in word 0 and never writes word 1. forwarded_target reads word 0 and treats any non-zero low nibble as a marker, so payloads such as Int 1, 3, -1, many floats and atom id 1 would read as forwarded, and writing a marker would destroy the payload. Making it safe needs a dedicated, zeroed marker word on every box, paid at every box allocation to save 16 bytes in a case that has not been observed.

Measured with reverted probes at a5f9e6702: across all 552 fixtures on run and interp (208 collections), no scalar-box root was copied and no root pointed into the middle of another object. A crafted program (scalar messages queued in a collecting child's mailbox) reaches the path; every root named its own box, with no duplicates.
title: A root's scalar box is copied per root, and needs no forwarding marker
